title: Keep Users Logged In Across Servers
statement: A ticket site runs four identical servers behind a load balancer. Users must stay logged in when a request lands on a different server. The security team also wants a logout to take effect immediately on every server. Which design fits best?
examples: User logs in on Server 1, then clicks Buy on Server 3
constraints: Four servers now, possibly more at peak
Logout must take effect at once

approaches.name: Store sessions in a shared session store that every server reads
approaches.label: best
approaches.time: About 1 ms to read a session from a nearby store (approximate)
approaches.space: One session record per logged-in user
approaches.why: Any server can read the session, and deleting it logs the user out everywhere at once. The store is an extra part to run and keep available.

approaches.name: Sticky sessions: the load balancer always sends a user to the same server
approaches.label: valid
approaches.space: Session stays in one server's memory
approaches.why: This keeps users logged in, so it works. Load becomes uneven, and if that server fails the users lose their sessions. Logout also has to reach the right server.

approaches.name: Give each user a signed token that holds the session and nothing is stored on the server
approaches.hint: Carry the data with the user
approaches.label: valid
approaches.space: The token travels with each request
approaches.why: This scales well and needs no shared store. A token that is already issued stays valid until it expires, so an immediate logout is hard without extra checks.

approaches.name: Keep sessions in each server's memory and hope users stay on one server
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Users are sent to different servers by the balancer, so they will be logged out at random.
